name: SnatchBot
tagline: No-code platform for building chatbots and voice assistants across web and messaging channels.
best_for: Support teams that want a chatbot without writing code
description:
SnatchBot is a browser-based platform for designing chatbots and voice assistants without programming. You assemble conversations in a drag-and-drop builder, define intents and entities, add quick replies, and publish the result to a website chat widget or to messaging apps such as Messenger, Telegram, Slack, Viber and Line. WhatsApp is supported through Twilio.

The aim is mostly customer service: answer repeat questions, take some load off a support queue, and hand the conversation to a human agent with the transcript attached when the bot gets stuck. Knowledge can be imported from FAQs, websites or files, and APIs and webhooks link it to CRMs and help desks. Analytics cover sessions, drop-offs and handoff rates. Plans and message limits change, so check the official site before choosing a tier.
use_steps: Create an account and start a new bot in the builder.
Map the common questions to intents and write the replies.
Import FAQ content and connect the channels you use.
Test with real queries, then review the analytics and fix gaps.
pros: Live agent handoff keeps the transcript
cons: Pricing tied to messaging, so costs need checking
Complex flows still take planning time
features: Publishing to web and messaging apps
use_cases: FAQ bot on a company website

name: Wordly
tagline: Live AI translation, captions and transcripts for meetings and events.
best_for: Organizations running multilingual meetings, webinars and events
description:
Wordly translates speech in real time for meetings and events. A speaker talks, and attendees read translated text or hear translated audio on their own phone or browser, in the language they pick. There are no interpreter booths or special hardware involved, which is the main practical difference from traditional simultaneous interpretation.

Beyond translation it produces same-language captions, searchable transcripts and session summaries, and it can plug into platforms such as Zoom, Webex, Microsoft Teams and Cvent. Optional glossaries help keep brand terms consistent, and it is built to handle many attendees and parallel sessions. The listing describes it as paid, with packages based on hours and attendees, so ask for current terms on the official site.

Add a glossary of names and product terms.
Share the attendee link or QR code and connect your meeting platform.
Run a short test session, then review the transcript afterwards.
cons: Paid only, no permanent free tool
Machine translation can miss nuance in technical talks
features: Live translation in dozens of languages
pricing_details: Wordly is paid, with packages based on hours and attendees. Trials may appear during promotions. Check the official site for current pricing.

name: Peec AI
tagline: Tracks how often your brand shows up in AI chatbot answers.
best_for: Marketers moving from classic SEO to AI search visibility
description:
Peec AI is an analytics platform for AI search. Instead of tracking Google rankings, it checks how often a brand is mentioned in answers from assistants such as ChatGPT, Perplexity, Claude and Gemini, and turns that into visibility metrics you can follow over time.

You define a set of prompts that matter to your market, and the tool shows which ones trigger your brand, how you compare with competitors, and which sources the AI engines cite. Monitoring can span several countries and languages in one workspace, and data can be exported or pushed to BI tools. The listing describes it as paid, with entry pricing and higher tiers for more prompts and markets, so confirm current plans on the official site.

Write the prompts your customers might ask an AI assistant.
Let it collect answers and review visibility and position.
Check which sources are cited and plan content around the gaps.
cons: Results depend on the prompt set you choose

name: Polymer
tagline: No-code BI that turns spreadsheets into interactive dashboards.
best_for: Non-technical teams who want dashboards without SQL
description:
Polymer is a cloud-based business intelligence tool aimed at people who work in spreadsheets rather than SQL. You upload a CSV, XLSX or Google Sheets file, or connect a data source, and it builds an interactive dashboard that can be filtered and shared.

AI suggests charts and writes short explanations of what the data shows, and a natural language search box lets you ask a question and get a chart back. Connectors include Google Analytics 4, Google Ads and Facebook Ads, and automatic syncing is available on higher tiers. It suits marketing, e-commerce, operations and finance teams. A free plan exists, with paid tiers above it, but check the official site for current prices.

Review the charts it suggests and adjust them.
Ask questions in plain language to explore the data.
Share the dashboard with your team.
pros: No SQL or BI training needed
cons: Less depth than enterprise BI platforms
features: Encryption in transit and at rest
pricing_details: Polymer has a free plan and paid tiers with yearly billing options. Prices change, so check the official site.

name: Sisense
tagline: API-first analytics platform for embedding governed BI in products.
best_for: Product teams and data leaders embedding analytics in applications
description:
Sisense is a business intelligence platform built around embedding. Teams use its SDK, JavaScript components and REST APIs to put charts, metrics and narrative summaries inside their own products and workflows, rather than sending users to a separate BI portal.

It connects to cloud warehouses and lakes such as Snowflake, BigQuery and Databricks, with live querying or caching for speed. A semantic layer keeps metrics consistent, and governance covers role-based access, row-level security, lineage, audit logs and SSO. Business users can ask questions in plain language, and alerts can fire to Slack, email or webhooks when KPIs change. It can run as Sisense Cloud or in your own cloud. Pricing depends on scale, so contact the vendor.

Build a semantic model with governed metrics.
Create dashboards or embed components through the SDK.
Set roles, security rules and KPI alerts.
use_cases: Customer-facing analytics in a SaaS app

name: ThoughtSpot
tagline: AI analytics platform for searching live cloud data in plain language.
description:
ThoughtSpot lets people ask questions of their data in natural language and get charts back. It connects directly to cloud warehouses such as Snowflake, BigQuery and Databricks, so answers come from live data rather than extracts. Spotter, its AI analyst, explains results and handles follow-up questions.

Results can be pinned to Liveboards, interactive dashboards with drill-down, KPI monitoring and alerts. Data teams curate models for consistency, while Analyst Studio offers SQL, Python, R and notebooks for deeper work. Product teams can embed analytics via the ThoughtSpot Everywhere SDK. Governance includes roles, row-level security, lineage and audit logs. The listing says pricing is per user and per query depending on scale, with a free trial, so check the official site.

Have the data team build and curate a model.
Ask questions in plain language or via Spotter.
Pin answers to a Liveboard and set alerts.
pros: Natural language search on live data
cons: Answer quality depends on a well-curated model
